Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can produce an itemized invoice with separate line items for base SKU, reserved capacity surcharge, and the channel uplift; and yes, the DocuSign envelope can be configured so the signed terms reference the same itemized schedule.

I'll outline what we typically provide and call out one option you should consider:

- Invoice layout: we issue a PDF invoice that supports line-level descriptions and also include machine-readable metadata (custom fields) that list SKU id, SKU description, quantity, unit price, tax code, and an external reference (your PO#).
- Channel uplift: two operational options:
  1) Pass-through line: Redwood invoices the base and the uplift as separate lines (recommended by your auditors). The uplift has its own GL code so you can track partner fees explicitly.
  2) Net unit price: we fold uplift into the unit price; simpler invoicing but harder for partner reconciliation.

Operational implications: if you choose pass-through, accounting will see two invoice lines, but it also means the uplift is subject to the same payment terms. If you need the uplift to be payable to a third party address or via partner invoice, that's a slightly different flow (we can provide a reseller invoice path but it requires partner onboarding details).

Connor, can you confirm the GL code name we use for channel uplift and whether the billing system will output it as a discrete CSV column? Irene / Vanessa — looping you for final wording in the invoice template.

I can attach an example invoice and the current private-offer line-items sheet; attaching now.
